1	# Plan: issue #187, a plan review rerun starts from the owner's revision
2	
3	Line numbers are from the worktree. "Facts" is `facts.md`; S is its Settled
4	section, U its Unresolved, O its For the owner.
5	
6	## Where this departs from the issue
7	
8	- The issue says the `revise` note "should survive a runner failure the
9	  same way an answered decision does". It already does, and nothing in
10	  the failure path touches it. The note is in the decision's
11	  `DecisionState::Answered { note }` and in `<subject>.feedback-<round>.md`
12	  beside the copy. `fail_attempt` (`dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7148`) touches no
13	  file, and the app deletes none (S, "The app does not touch the copy").
14	  The plan adds no storage for the note. It names the feedback file in the
15	  rerun question so the owner can find it.
16	- The issue's "newest plan the stage holds" has no counterpart in the
17	  code: `review_subject` (`scheduler.rs:10534`) takes the newest
18	  `Complete` attempt that wrote `plan`, and a `revise` edits the copy of
19	  an attempt that is never `Complete` until `finalize`. The plan adds the
20	  one case the issue is about (a failed attempt holding a finished owner
21	  revision), not a general rule.
22	- The investigation notes say a non-empty `Attempt.revisions` shows that
23	  the copy holds an owner revision. It does not (S, "Partial or finished
24	  revision"): `revise` pushes the `Revision` before sending the round and
25	  keeps it when the app refuses the round (`scheduler.rs:7607-7647`;
26	  only the feedback file is removed). The field's own doc comment at
27	  `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:348-349` says "popped when Switchboard refuses
28	  it", which the code does not do. The plan corrects the comment and does
29	  not change the behaviour. The evidence of a finished revision is the
30	  response file the planner writes.
31	- Not fixed, because the issue does not ask and it needs the app: the
32	  rerun's planner is still a clone of the plan stage's original session
33	  (`source`, S "`source` and the new planner"), so it has not seen the
34	  note either. It reviews the revised file, which contains the revision.
35	  Named under follow-ups.
36	
37	## The record
38	
39	One additive field. `Attempt.revised_from: Option<u32>` in
40	`dispatch/src/ticket.rs`, `#[serde(default)]`: for a plan review attempt, the
41	number of the earlier attempt of the same stage and context whose
42	owner-revised copy this attempt's copy was made from; none when it was made
43	from the plan stage's output. Written when the attempt is made in
44	`start_workflow` and never changed, as `carried_from` is. It is a decision
45	made once, so `show` and a restarted runner report what was done rather than
46	re-deriving it from files that may have changed. `new_attempt`
47	(`scheduler.rs:10277`) sets it `None`.
48	
49	`dispatch/src/store.rs`: `RECORD_VERSION` (`store.rs:26`) goes from the value
50	there at implementation time, plus one. Add the matching comment-only step in
51	`migrate` (`store.rs:452`), as the other steps that only add a defaulted
52	field do. Nothing is transformed. The store already refuses to write a newer
53	version. `crate::model` (`SCHEMA_VERSION`, `src/core/model.rs:12`) is not
54	touched. `docs/dispatch.md` has its per-version list near line 393: add the
55	paragraph there.
56	
57	Rehydration: `workflow_stage` re-reads the ticket every pass, and the chosen
58	copy is `attempts[n].artifacts[subject]` plus `revised_from`. A runner
59	restart between the `rerun` answer and the launch re-derives the choice with
60	the same function, from files that still exist (S: the app removes nothing).
61	
62	## The signals
63	
64	No new signal and nothing new from outside. The one new read is whether a
65	response file exists beside a failed attempt's copy
66	(`report::response_file`, `dispatch/src/report.rs:202`).
67	
68	Choosing the plan: replace `review_subject` (one caller, `start_workflow`
69	at `scheduler.rs:7465`; S "Plan readers") with
70	`plan_to_review(t, stage, ctx, subject)`, returning an owned struct
71	`{ path, session, revised_from: Option<u32>, skipped: Option<(u32, u32)> }`
72	(owned `PathBuf`s because `start_workflow` mutates `t.attempts` right after,
73	and a struct holding references into `t` would still be borrowed then).
74	
75	Walk `t.attempts` newest first by `Vec` position:
76	
77	1. A `Complete` attempt whose `artifacts` has `subject` ends the walk. Its
78	   `session` is the `source`, as today. Its path is the plan, unless step 2
79	   found a revised copy earlier in the walk.
80	2. A `Workflow` attempt of this `stage` and `ctx`, `Failed` or `Cancelled`,
81	   with `artifacts[subject]` a file on disk and a non-empty `revisions`, is a
82	   candidate. Take the highest `Revision.round` whose feedback file
83	   (`report::round_file`) still exists, since a refused round's file was
84	   removed. No such round: not a candidate. Its response file exists: the
85	   revision is finished, and this is the revised copy (first one wins).
86	   Otherwise the planner clone may still be editing, so record it in
87	   `skipped` as `(attempt n, round)` and keep walking.
88	3. Anything else is passed over.
89	
90	Why these choices:
91	- U2 (is a failed copy ever mid-edit) is unresolved and nothing here can
92	  answer it, so the default does not assume either way. An unfinished
93	  revision is not used; the plan stage's output is, and the question says
94	  why. The enhancement, the revised copy, is only taken when the response
95	  file proves it finished. Both branches give a working rerun.
96	- U1 (can the plan stage rerun after review/1 failed): ranking by `Vec`
97	  position makes a later `Complete` plan win either way, because the walk
98	  stops at it before reaching review/1. Right in both branches (a fresh plan
99	  supersedes an old revision). A unit test pins it.
100	- O1 (was the file intact on the owner's disk): a missing or non-file copy
101	  fails the `is_file` check in step 2 and the walk falls back to the plan
102	  stage's output. Same code whichever the owner reports.
103	- Only owner revisions are carried, not the reviewer-round edits a failed
104	  attempt's planner made. Those are not owner input, and today's behaviour
105	  of starting again from the plan stage's output stays for them. A later
106	  failure without a new `revise` therefore still reaches review/1's
107	  revision (review/2 has no `revisions` and is passed over).
108	
109	## The actions and effects
110	
111	No new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The wire to Switchboard is unchanged:
112	`start_workflow` copies `plan_to_review().path` to the new attempt's
113	directory (`scheduler.rs:7466-7471`) and sends the same `Body::WorkflowStart
114	{ source, plan, .. }`. Add the call's `revised_from` to the attempt it pushes
115	(`:7480`) and log one `info` line naming the file chosen and, when
116	`skipped` is set, the unfinished revision passed over.
117	
118	`rerun_carries` (`scheduler.rs:9382`) returns `String` instead of
119	`&'static str` and gains an arm for a `Workflow` attempt (today it returns
120	"" there). Both callers format it already (`:7266`, `:9373`). It calls
121	`plan_to_review` with the attempt's stage and context, and the subject name
122	from `a.artifacts.keys().next()`. It adds one sentence:
123	- revised: "The rerun reviews the owner-revised copy from `<stage>/<n>` at
124	  `<path>`; your note for round `<r>` is at `<feedback file>`."
125	- skipped: "`<stage>/<n>` holds a revision (round `<r>`) the planner had not
126	  finished, so the rerun reviews the plan stage's output at `<path>`; your
127	  note is at `<feedback file>`."
128	- otherwise: "The rerun reviews the plan stage's output at `<path>`."
129	- an `Err` from `plan_to_review` gives "", as now.
130	
131	The question is a snapshot (`ensure_decision`, `scheduler.rs:3225`, dedups on
132	stage, name and attempt, not on text), so it states what the choice is when
133	asked. `revised_from` on the launched attempt is what `show` reports.
134	
135	Also fix the `revisions` doc comment (`ticket.rs:348`): a refused round
136	leaves the `Revision` and removes only the feedback file.
137	
138	## The UI
139	
140	CLI `show` only. The wire type is additive.
141	
142	- `dispatch-control/src/lib.rs:586`: `LaneFile` gains `prior:
143	  Option<PriorCopy>`, with a new `PriorCopy { n: u32, path: PathBuf }`
144	  (`Default`, `#[serde(default)]` like its neighbours). `LaneFile` is
145	  `#[serde(default)]`, so older readers and the app, which reads only
146	  `plan_reviewing`, `plan_reviewed`, `plan_round` and `plan_stage`
147	  (`src/ui/ticket.rs:427-431`), are unaffected (S, "Wire types").
148	- `ticket_paths` (`dispatch/src/serve.rs`, the `plan_files` build near the
149	  `LaneFile { .. }` literal) fills `prior` from the attempt's
150	  `revised_from`: that attempt's `artifacts[subject]`.
151	- `print_lane_files` (`dispatch/src/main.rs:896`) prints, under the plan line
152	  and whether or not the review is still open: `(started from the owner's
153	  revision in <stage>/<n>: <path>)`. This answers "which is the reviewed copy
154	  and which is a prior revision" for the case in the issue: the listed path is
155	  the reviewed copy, and the line gives the revision it began from.
156	- The ticket page's Plan tab in the app and the Swift client are not changed.
157	  Added to the design.md gap list below. (`grep planFiles|plan_files client/`
158	  finds nothing, S.)
159	
160	## The tests
161	
162	Integration, `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs`, next to
163	`a_failed_review_run_fails_the_attempt_and_a_rerun_starts_a_new_run` (`:3257`)
164	using `at_finalize`, `revise` (`:3417`) and `review_run_fails` (`:3249`):
165	
166	1. Revised then failed then rerun: after `revise`, the test plays the
167	   planner (edit the copy, write `response_file(copy, 2)`), fails the run,
168	   answers `rerun`. Assert the attempt-2 copy has the revised text,
169	   `revised_from == Some(1)`, the `WorkflowStart` plan is the attempt-2 copy,
170	   its `source` is the plan stage's session, and the rerun question names
171	   review/1's copy and the feedback file. `show --json` has `prior`
172	   pointing at review/1's copy.
173	2. Unfinished: same without the response file. Attempt 2's copy equals
174	   `plan/1`'s output, `revised_from` is none, the question says the revision
175	   was unfinished.
176	3. Refused round: the fake refuses `workflow.object`, so the feedback file
177	   is gone and the `Revision` stays; the rerun starts from the plan stage's
178	   output without the "unfinished" sentence.
179	4. The existing test and its siblings: no revise, so the copy is the plan
180	   stage's output. Update any assertion on the exact rerun question text;
181	   the question now ends with the "reviews the plan stage's output" sentence.
182	
183	Unit, in `scheduler.rs` beside the plan-reader tests (about `:12449`):
184	`plan_to_review` on built tickets: (a) a `Complete` plan only; (b) revised
185	and finished failed review before it; (c) a `Complete` plan attempt appended
186	after the failed review wins (U1); (d) review/2 failed with no revisions
187	after a finished review/1: review/1's copy is chosen again; (e) a
188	`Cancelled` attempt counts as a `Failed` one; (f) the copy file missing
189	falls back (O1). `store.rs`: a version-28-era record (use the previous
190	`RECORD_VERSION` fixture style at `:1104`) loads with `revised_from` none and
191	is written at the new version. `serve.rs` tests (about `:1590-1710`):
192	`ticket_paths` sets `prior`. A `main.rs` test for `print_lane_files` if one
193	exists for the `reviewing` line; otherwise cover it through the integration
194	test's `show` output.
195	
196	## Docs
197	
198	- `docs/dispatch.md` near `:393`: the version paragraph.
199	- `docs/design.md`: the plan review rerun paragraph (`:1783-1790`, "a rerun
200	  kills the old run's agents and starts a fresh run"): add that the fresh
201	  run starts from the failed attempt's owner-revised copy when its
202	  response file shows the revision finished. Under the Dispatch ticket page
203	  section (`:2135`) list the gap: the Plan tab does not show `prior`.
204	- `README.md`: no new file, so no Layout change; no new environment
205	  variable.
206	- `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased: "A plan review rerun after a failed
207	  attempt starts from the owner's `revise` copy when the planner finished it,
208	  and the rerun question and `show` say which copy it reviews."
209	
210	## One commit
211	
212	Message: `Dispatch: a plan review rerun starts from the failed attempt's owner-revised copy (#187)`
213	
214	Contract additions (copy into the commit message body):
215	- `dispatch::ticket::Attempt.revised_from: Option<u32>`, `#[serde(default)]`;
216	  dispatch `RECORD_VERSION` bumped (value in `store.rs` at implementation
217	  time, plus one) with a defaulted-field step in `store::migrate`.
218	- `dispatch_control::PriorCopy { n: u32, path: PathBuf }` and
219	  `dispatch_control::LaneFile.prior: Option<PriorCopy>`, additive on the wire.
220	- Internal: `plan_to_review` replaces `review_subject`; `rerun_carries`
221	  returns `String`. No `AppAction`, `Effect`, port or `model.rs` change.
222	
223	## For the owner, after this lands
224	
225	- The rerun's planner is a clone of the original planner and has not seen the
226	  `revise` note (S). Giving it the note means changing what
227	  `workflow.start` sends or clones, in the app. Needs a spike and a contract
228	  change; not in this commit.
229	- The app's Plan tab does not show `prior` yet.
230	- O1 and U2 are unanswered. The plan works either way; the owner's data
231	  directory would show whether any real failure left a half-written copy, and
232	  if so whether the planner should be stopped when an attempt fails.

# Facts: issue #187

The issue and the investigation claim nothing about a browser, platform, crate, protocol or tool outside this tree. Every open question is about the tree, so no web search was run and no spike was written (git status is empty). Line numbers are from this worktree.

## Settled

Plan readers (open question 1):
- `review_subject` has one caller, `start_workflow`. It reads `t.attempts` newest first by `Vec` position and keeps only `AttemptState::Complete`. `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7465`, `:10534-10547`.
- Every other reader of the plan goes through `Ticket::input_where`, which is also Complete-only and skips `forgotten`. These are `lane_input` (`scheduler.rs:10843`), then `lane_plan`, `lane_plans` and `plan_clause`, and the prompt variables `vars_for` (`:10776`). `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:1452-1462`.
- Report plan lists use `lane_files` (`dispatch/src/report.rs:300`). `serve.rs:587` reads only `notes`.
- Changing `review_subject` alone leaves all of these on Complete attempts, so downstream stages and prompts never see an unfinalized or failed copy.
- Making `input_where` count a failed review attempt's copy would change what implement and code review are handed. That is wider than the issue.
- `Ticket::shown_where` also takes an open workflow attempt, never a failed one. `ticket.rs:1476-1488`. It is display only (`scheduler.rs:10917-10919`).

The app does not touch the copy (question 2):
- The app has no code that deletes or moves the plan copy or its feedback and response files. `RemoveWorkflow` only drops the run record and probes: `src/core/workflow.rs:1009-1031`.
- `start_workflow` in the app only reads `plan` and clones the source's transcript. It writes nothing to that path: `src/core/workflow.rs:289-345`.
- The only `remove_file` calls in `src/` are `app.rs:1497` (`remove_quietly`, unrelated), the hook binary's own files, the updater, and a PNG temp in `ui/document.rs`. `grep remove_file|remove_dir_all|rename src` found no others.
- Dispatch's `fail_attempt` also touches no files (investigation item 6).
- So review/1's `plan.md` is intact when attempt 2 starts. Dispatch deletes one file only: the owner's feedback file for a round the app refused (`scheduler.rs:7640-7647`).

Partial or finished revision (question 3):
- `revise` writes the feedback file, then pushes the `Revision` onto `Attempt.revisions`, then sends `WorkflowObject` (`scheduler.rs:7607-7628`).
- If the app refuses the round, the feedback file is removed but the `Revision` stays (`:7640-7647`). A non-empty `revisions` therefore does not prove the planner revised anything.
- `revise` runs only while the run is `Converged` or `AtCap` (`:7600-7606`).
- The investigation's suggestion that "non-empty `revisions` says the copy holds an owner revision" does not hold. A finished revision is evidenced by the response file `<subject>.response-<round>.md` beside the copy, which the planner writes.

Attempt order (question 4):
- Attempts are appended to `t.attempts` (`scheduler.rs:7479`), and every reader above orders by `Vec` position. `started_ms` and `ended_ms` exist (`ticket.rs:375-376`) but no reader uses them to rank attempts.
- Any "newest plan" rule built on position is well defined, with ties impossible.

`source` and the new planner (question 5):
- The app requires `source` to be a Claude Code session with a transcript and clones it as the planner (`src/core/workflow.rs:306-322`).
- `review_subject` returns the plan stage's session as `source`. The new planner is therefore a clone of the original planner, which has seen neither the `revise` note nor the revision.
- The reviser's context lives only in review/1's run planner clone (an app record the failed run leaves behind).
- The owner's note survives on disk in the decision's `DecisionState::Answered { note }` and in `<subject>.feedback-<round>.md`. The `OWNER_ROUND_HEADING` text is in the feedback file.

Wire types (question 6):
- `LaneFile` is `#[serde(default)]`, so a new field is additive on the wire (`dispatch-control/src/lib.rs:584-599`).
- The app reads only `plan_reviewing`, `plan_reviewed`, `plan_round` and `plan_stage` (`src/ui/ticket.rs:427-431`).
- The CLI reads `plan_files` through `print_lane_files` (`dispatch/src/main.rs:896`, `:982`).
- `grep planFiles|plan_files|reviewing client/` found nothing in the Swift client. The investigation's mention of `TicketFileView` could not be matched to a use of these fields.
- A new `LaneFile` field or a new `PathsView` list should be additive and break none of the three readers.

The `[run]` question:
- The fake already reproduces the path up to the rerun: `a_failed_review_run_fails_the_attempt_and_a_rerun_starts_a_new_run` (`dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3257`), with `review_run_fails` (`:3249`).
- Whether attempt 2 starts from `plan/1` follows from the read above (Complete filter at `scheduler.rs:10537`; no step marks a failed attempt Complete).
- The plan stage is Complete in that test, and the test's review attempt has no revise before the failure.
- A new test only needs a `revise` step (helper at `first_slice.rs:3417`) between `at_review_run` and `review_run_fails`. This is a test the plan writes, not a question for a spike.

## Unresolved

U1. Can the plan stage itself be rerun after review/1 failed, so `plan/2` is appended after review/1?
- Tried: read `workflow_stage`, `review_subject` and `start_workflow` only. I did not trace the stage-ordering code.
- Branch where it can: a "newest plan" rule by `Vec` position then prefers `plan/2` over review/1's revision. That is correct, since a fresh plan supersedes the old revision. The plan must test this order.
- Branch where it cannot: the rule is simply "newest of failed review copy and Complete plan".
- Build to: rank by `Vec` position in both cases. Add a test with a later `plan` attempt, and do not wait on this line.

U2. Is a failed attempt's copy ever mid-edit when the rerun starts? The planner clone may still be running when `poll_workflow` sees `no such run` or a failed state.
- Tried: nothing runs here (needs a live app and planner), and the code does not stop the planner on `fail_attempt`.
- Build to: if the planner is quiet, take the failed copy. If not, the plan cannot tell. So the rule that copies a failed attempt's `plan.md` must require a finished revision. The evidence available is the response file for the latest `Revision.round` on that attempt. Otherwise fall back to the Complete plan, and the rerun question and `show` must say which file is used.

- If the owner reports the copy was empty or reverted, the plan adds nothing different. It falls back to the Complete plan and names it in the rerun question and `show`.

The owner round is round N+1 on the same file (`revise` uses `view.round + 1`, `scheduler.rs:7627`, and `round_file(&subject, round)` beside the same copy). Neither facts.md nor the tree supports separating the two kinds of edit. Either drop the claim and say the rerun reviews everything the failed attempt's planner had done up to the finished owner round, or cite what separates them. This also changes the rerun question text (the "owner-revised copy" wording promises less than it delivers) and the CHANGELOG line.

The planner's respond prompt (`src/core/model.rs:279-284`) says "provide a response in markdown at {response}. Accept valid items by updating the plan". It does not require the plan edit first, and the app counts a round as responded when the response file appears (`src/core/workflow.rs:663-668`). A planner that writes the response and then edits is still mid-edit with the file present. This is the same unresolved U2 the plan says it does not depend on, and the plan does depend on it for its "proves it finished" claim. Name this as the implementer's first check (read the respond template and note that the response can land before the last edit), or word the default as "the planner has answered the round", not "finished". The fallback to the plan stage's output remains the safe default, so no new mechanism is needed, only an honest premise.

The plan's own text says the question will claim "had not finished" for both. Nothing in the facts or tree distinguishes a dead planner from a slow one. The wording should say "no response file was found", the observable fact, not a state of the planner.

I wrote four objections to the feedback file, all about premises. Nothing in the plan breaches a hard rule, and every line reference I checked matched the worktree. The facts file raises no outside-the-tree questions, so I ran no web searches.
